publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving the Product Design Process
abstract: The University of Southampton Central Design Service (CDS) was set up 26 years ago, to provide an engineering design service for any department within the University, especially those with no such capability of their own. The CDS has used Computer Aided Design/Draughting for the past 10 years and all work is now produced solely on CAD, pencil drawing having been phased out seven years ago. Since the decision to switch to computer draughting a great deal of expertise has been built up in the use of CAD; both two and three dimensional. This expertise is detailed in the paper.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Managing product design-a revolution in the making
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving the Product Design Process
abstract: The advance of industrial practice is seldom smooth. Progress is more likely to take place in quantum leaps, or even by simple fits and starts. Established ways and means often continue unchallenged for years on end, until the perceived benefits from change are such that a deluge of activity is released. The forces of inertia are then swamped (with results that are usually but not always beneficial) and some form of revolution is unleashed. Forecasting revolution is of little use unless pointers can be given as to outcomes. Although making predictions is notoriously risky, some of the outcomes of the coming revolution in managing design are already discernible and form the basis of this paper.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving the Product Design Process
abstract: The design process is an iterative procedure which refines the original design concept through a process of evaluation and test. The process can be expensive and inefficient in the use of resources and mistakes made during the process can lead to the product being over budget and late for the market. DPI is a computer aided analysis of the design process, which uses the IDEF functional architecture diagraming method to model the design process. The IDEF diagrams are then evaluated and scored to determine the changes required to improve the effectiveness of the design process.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
